A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SuffixDecoding work. All main-text and appendix pages support comparison; text extraction, rendered pages, and matching figures and tables reveal no material reading gaps.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original benchmark measurements, end-to-end SWE-Bench experiments, simulated ablations, and empirical entropy analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds measured memory and operation costs and hybrid-threshold sensitivity results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the global and per-request suffix trees, greedy expansion, frequency-based scoring, adaptive speculation lengths, and threshold-based EAGLE fallback are unchanged. New tuning guidance and suggested eviction or batching integrations do not establish implemented method changes.

E1.justification: SWE-Bench, AgenticSQL, Spec-Bench, WildChat, Magicoder, and SpiderSQL coverage is retained. V3 identifies the MT-Bench origin of existing Spec-Bench categories; its new scaling and threshold analyses use retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain vanilla decoding, EAGLE variants, PLD, and Token Recycling, with the same unavailable SWE-Bench results. Newly cited TurboSpec and AdaServe are discussed as integration possibilities, without evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: New appendix analyses introduce tree-size settings from 1,000 to 20,000 SWE-Bench entries and fallback-threshold sweeps on Spec-Bench and AgenticSQL. Previously reported models, batch sizes, metrics, and serving configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds targeted analyses of memory, update and lookup costs as trees grow, and performance sensitivity to the hybrid fallback threshold. Existing tree-component ablations, cache-size studies, distribution-shift tests, and entropy analysis are retained.

E5.justification: No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation changes are documented. The added tables continue reporting averages or point values without new uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Original figures, detailed benchmark values, and Table 1 are unchanged. New Table 2 reports, for example, 6150 MB for 572 million tokens, with 4.04 microseconds per token update and 11.64 microseconds per speculated-token lookup. Tables 3-4 add threshold-dependent speedups, while redisplaying some existing results.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds an explicit capacity derivation: measured memory per token, a 144 GB CPU-memory budget, and an assumed 5000 tokens/second yield approximately 31 days before filling memory. The original probability definitions and algorithmic equations remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution: adaptive, model-free speculation exploiting repetitive agentic workloads, with optional model-based fallback. Headline claims, including 5.3× decoding speedup and up to 4.5× end-to-end speedup, are unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds conditional cache-lifetime estimates, workload-specific threshold recommendations, and discussion of batching applicability. Some new interpretations need qualification: Table 3 gives 2.37×, 2.31×, and 2.50× for thresholds 5, 6, and 7; Table 4 rebounds from 3.22× at threshold 3 to 3.66× at 7 despite the described progressive degradation.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project-page link, concrete memory and maintenance-cost measurements, and practical threshold-selection guidance. Existing implementation and hardware disclosures in Appendix A.1.1 are retained; the PDFs do not establish implementation of the suggested eviction or batching extensions.

R1.justification: V3 adds multi-token prediction and blockwise decoding references, MT-Bench attribution, and discussion of compatibility with TurboSpec and AdaServe. It removes Agentless, Chain of Agents, and DeepResearcher citations. These are limited changes around the retained positioning as speculation for repetitive agentic workloads.

P1.justification: V3 condenses introductory and background passages, merges the former Related Works section into Section 2, and adds benchmark explanations and appendix cross-references. Most method and evaluation prose remains intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 2-4, front-page project/code links, and a conference footer, with local reflow and a separate appendix start. Figures 1-9 and the original table structures are retained without substantive graphical revisions.

improvement.justification: The new measurements substantiate memory costs and provide threshold-tuning evidence absent from v2, modestly improving practical completeness. These benefits are tempered by overstated threshold trends in Appendix B.1, particularly the claimed progressive degradation contradicted by Table 4. The original method and principal experimental evidence remain unchanged.
